42038: The sources don't give its thickness or length (OPEN-QUESTIONS.md); its stiffness E b t³/12 L sets the balance's swing. Within −5 % to +11 % of the drawn spring's (0.411-0.434 mm thick at the drawn 13.55 mm width and 1064 mm length; about 0.85-1.00 N·m fully wound) the balance swings the manual's 1⅜-1½ turns (247.5-270°), and the escapement's rate changes -0.09 to +0.16 s a day, which the timing takes up. Measure the strip before fitting it: one 0.375 mm thick, the same length, swings the balance only 213° (it runs, 0.69 s a day slow before timing). (The drive taken to scale with the spring's stiffness, the fusee evening it as drawn; tools/tolerances.js)
42087: The sources don't give its spring's section (OPEN-QUESTIONS.md). Its stiffness goes as its thickness cubed: up to 1.9 times the drawn spring's (0.098 mm thick, the drawn 0.079 over 3.82 mm to the point of flexure) the balance still swings 247.5° or more; stiffer, unlocking takes too much of the impulse. Its work sets no lower limit (with none, 263°): set its preload by the manual's test (Op. 78: a 0.770 g weight on the locking jewel just parts the spring from its stop button). Whether a thinner spring brings the detent back in time to lock the next tooth is not computed. (tools/tolerances.js)
